lines.en: Hannah, we spent all day looking for that old radio, and every stall at this market sold the same cheap souvenirs.
lines.pt: Hannah, passamos o dia inteiro procurando aquele rádio antigo, e todas as barracas deste mercado vendiam as mesmas lembrancinhas baratas.

lines.en: I know. I wasted two hours asking the vendors about it, and half of them did not understand what I meant.
lines.pt: Eu sei. Perdi duas horas perguntando aos vendedores sobre ele, e metade deles nem entendeu o que eu queria dizer.

lines.en: Maybe we should stop wasting time in this hall. My father’s birthday is on Saturday, and I still have nothing for him.
lines.pt: Talvez devêssemos parar de perder tempo neste pavilhão. O aniversário do meu pai é no sábado, e ainda não tenho nada para ele.

lines.en: Wait, someone told me the best antiques are at the back, near the river entrance. Have you been there yet?
lines.pt: Espere, alguém me disse que as melhores antiguidades ficam nos fundos, perto da entrada do rio. Você já foi lá?

lines.en: Not yet. Honestly, I have trouble finding anything useful in big markets. Last year I spent a whole weekend hunting for one lamp.
lines.pt: Ainda não. Sinceramente, tenho dificuldade em achar algo útil em mercados grandes. No ano passado passei um fim de semana inteiro caçando um único abajur.

lines.en: And did you find it? I hope the lamp was worth all that time, because I hate wasting weekends like that.
lines.pt: E você achou? Espero que o abajur tenha valido todo esse tempo, porque odeio desperdiçar fins de semana assim.

lines.en: Eventually, yes, but it cost me a fortune. This time I would rather haggle for a fair price and go home early.
lines.pt: Por fim, sim, mas me custou uma fortuna. Desta vez prefiro pechinchar por um preço justo e voltar cedo para casa.

lines.en: Fair enough. Look, that man near the fountain is selling old radios. He seems to be busy repairing one right now.
lines.pt: Justo. Olhe, aquele homem perto da fonte vende rádios antigos. Parece que ele está ocupado consertando um agora mesmo.

lines.en: You are right! Excuse me, how much is the green one? It looks just like the radio my father had as a boy.
lines.pt: Você tem razão! Com licença, quanto custa o verde? Ele parece exatamente com o rádio que meu pai tinha quando menino.

lines.en: He says eighty dollars, but it needs a new speaker. Do you really want to pay that much for something broken?
lines.pt: Ele diz oitenta dólares, mas precisa de um alto-falante novo. Você quer mesmo pagar tanto por algo quebrado?

lines.en: Yes, because my father will love fixing it himself. Thanks for not giving up, Hannah. The whole day was worth it.
lines.pt: Sim, porque meu pai vai adorar consertá-lo sozinho. Obrigada por não desistir, Hannah. O dia todo valeu a pena.

facts.label: Tempo gasto
facts.sub: We spent all day looking. I wasted an hour waiting.

facts.label: spent all day looking
facts.sub: Use spend + expressão de tempo + verbo com -ing: We spent all day looking for it. Depois de spend o verbo não leva to nem for. O passado de spend é spent.

facts.label: wasted time waiting
facts.sub: Waste significa perder ou desperdiçar: I wasted two hours asking vendors. Também serve para dinheiro: waste money buying things. Use o -ing depois do tempo.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: We spent all day looking for it is correct.
We say “I spent two hours to wait”.
Waste time means to use time badly.

group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: We spent all day looking for it is correct. → Verdadeiro (Spend + time + -ing.)
We say “I spent two hours to wait”. → Falso (Use waiting, not to wait.)
Waste time means to use time badly. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A day at the market · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a hot Saturday in Houston. Nell and Hannah enter a huge market. They need a gift for her father. Nell wants an old radio. Hannah promises to help. The morning disappears quickly.

“Hannah, we spent all day looking for that old radio, and every stall at this market sold the same cheap souvenirs.” says Nell. “I know. I wasted two hours asking the vendors about it, and half of them did not understand what I meant.” says Hannah. “Maybe we should stop wasting time in this hall. My father’s birthday is on Saturday, and I still have nothing for him.” says Nell.
